# Local Services campaigns Stay organized with collections Save and categorize content based on your preferences.

![Spark icon](/_static/images/icons/spark.svg)

## Page Summary

outlined\_flag

*   Local Services campaigns on Google allow businesses to advertise and receive leads directly from potential customers.
    
*   The Google Ads API supports retrieving, editing status and budget, setting bidding strategies (ManualCpa, MaximizeConversions), setting ad schedules, setting location targeting, and targeting specific service types for Local Services campaigns.
    
*   You can submit feedback and rating for leads using the `ProvideLeadFeedback()` method and inspect the `lead_feedback_submitted` field.
    
*   Creating and removing Local Services campaigns, as well as operations on sub-entities like ad groups, ads, or criteria within these campaigns, are not supported by the Google Ads API.
    
*   Read-only report resources in the Google Ads API provide access to data from Local Services Ads, including details about leads, lead conversations, business verification artifacts, geographic and categorical license and insurance data, and employee information.
    

[Local Services campaigns](https://support.google.com/localservices/answer/6224841) let you advertise your business on Google and receive leads directly from potential customers. This guide summarizes the supported operations and restrictions in the Google Ads API.

## Supported operations

The Google Ads API supports the following operations for Local Services campaigns.

### Retrieve Local Services campaigns and budgets

Local Services campaigns and budgets can be retrieved using the [`GoogleAdsService.Search`](https://developers.google.com/google-ads/api/reference/rpc/v26/GoogleAdsService/Search) or [`GoogleAdsService.SearchStream`](https://developers.google.com/google-ads/api/reference/rpc/v26/GoogleAdsService/SearchStream) method to query for [`Campaign`](https://developers.google.com/google-ads/api/reference/rpc/v26/Campaign) resources where `advertising_channel_type = 'LOCAL_SERVICES'`. Here is an example:

```
SELECT
  campaign.id,
  campaign.status,
  campaign_budget.id,
  campaign_budget.period,
  campaign_budget.amount_micros,
  campaign_budget.type
FROM campaign
WHERE campaign.advertising_channel_type = 'LOCAL_SERVICES'
```

**Note:** Starting in **`v24`**, you can retrieve and update existing Local Services Performance Max campaigns (`advertising_channel_type = 'PERFORMANCE_MAX'` and `campaign.pmax_campaign_settings.local_services_enabled = true`) created in the UI by accounts on the allowlist. Starting in **`v26`**, you can also [create new Local Services Performance Max campaigns](https://developers.google.com/google-ads/api/docs/campaigns/local-service-campaigns#create-campaign) through the API. See [Local Services Performance Max campaigns](https://developers.google.com/google-ads/api/docs/campaigns/local-service-campaigns#pmax-campaigns), the [Performance Max for pay-per-lead goals guide](https://developers.google.com/google-ads/api/performance-max/pay-per-lead), and the [Performance Max campaign level performance guide](https://developers.google.com/google-ads/api/performance-max/campaign-reporting#pmax-local-services) for details.

### Edit Local Services campaigns

You can update the campaign's [`status`](https://developers.google.com/google-ads/api/reference/rpc/v26/Campaign#status) and the associated campaign budget's [`amount_micros`](https://developers.google.com/google-ads/api/reference/rpc/v26/CampaignBudget#amount_micros) fields.

### Set the bidding strategy

You can set the following bidding strategies as the standard bidding strategy of Local Services campaigns:

*   [`ManualCpa`](https://developers.google.com/google-ads/api/reference/rpc/v26/ManualCpa) by setting the field [`manual_cpa`](https://developers.google.com/google-ads/api/reference/rpc/v26/Campaign#manual_cpa)
    
    You can set the bids of `ManualCpa` through [`LocalServicesCampaignSettings.category_bids`](https://developers.google.com/google-ads/api/reference/rpc/v26/Campaign.LocalServicesCampaignSettings#category_bids%5B%5D). You can retrieve and set `LocalServicesCampaignSettings` of Local Services campaigns through [`Campaign.local_services_campaign_settings`](https://developers.google.com/google-ads/api/reference/rpc/v26/Campaign#local_services_campaign_settings).
    
*   [`MaximizeConversions`](https://developers.google.com/google-ads/api/reference/rpc/v26/MaximizeConversions) by setting the field [`maximize_conversions`](https://developers.google.com/google-ads/api/reference/rpc/v26/Campaign#maximize_conversions)
    

### Set an ad schedule as a campaign criterion

You can set an ad schedule for a Local Services campaign as a campaign criterion.

Create an [`AdScheduleInfo`](https://developers.google.com/google-ads/api/reference/rpc/v26/AdScheduleInfo) and set it to the [`ad_schedule`](https://developers.google.com/google-ads/api/reference/rpc/v26/CampaignCriterion#ad_schedule) of the `CampaignCriterion` that is sent to the Google Ads API, using [`CampaignCriterionService.MutateCampaignCriteria`](https://developers.google.com/google-ads/api/reference/rpc/v26/CampaignCriterionService/MutateCampaignCriteria).

### Set location targeting

To enable location targeting for a Local Services campaign, add a [`LocationInfo`](https://developers.google.com/google-ads/api/reference/rpc/v26/LocationInfo) and set it to the [`location`](https://developers.google.com/google-ads/api/reference/rpc/v26/CampaignCriterion#location) field of the `CampaignCriterion` that is sent to the Google Ads API, using [`CampaignCriterionService.MutateCampaignCriteria`](https://developers.google.com/google-ads/api/reference/rpc/v26/CampaignCriterionService/MutateCampaignCriteria). For more details, see [Location targeting](https://developers.google.com/google-ads/api/docs/targeting/location-targeting).

### Target specific service types

To enable targeting for a specific service type, create a [`LocalServiceIdInfo`](https://developers.google.com/google-ads/api/reference/rpc/v26/LocalServiceIdInfo) with one of the [Local Services category IDs](https://developers.google.com/google-ads/api/data/codes-formats#local_services_ids), set it on the [`local_service_id`](https://developers.google.com/google-ads/api/reference/rpc/v26/CampaignCriterion#local_service_id) field of a [`CampaignCriterion`](https://developers.google.com/google-ads/api/reference/rpc/v26/CampaignCriterion), and submit it using [`CampaignCriterionService.MutateCampaignCriteria`](https://developers.google.c

## What is a google local services ads reporting tool?

A google local services ads reporting tool consolidates lead data, call recordings, message threads, and conversion metrics from Google Local Services Ads into dashboard views that help local businesses optimize their advertising spend. Unlike traditional Google Ads, Local Services Ads operate on a pay-per-lead model where you are charged $5–$150 per qualified lead depending on your service category and market competition.

The core challenge with Local Services Ads is lead quality variance. Research from BrightLocal shows that 35% of Local Services leads never convert to actual customers due to poor qualification, pricing mismatches, or scheduling conflicts. Without proper tracking, contractors spend $2,000–$8,000 monthly on LSA leads that generate zero revenue. The right reporting tool identifies which lead sources, times, and service categories produce the highest customer lifetime value.

This guide covers 5 reporting platforms for Google Local Services Ads, 15 metrics every local service business should track, and step-by-step setup instructions for automated reporting. We also compare built-in Google tools with third-party analytics platforms and AI-powered solutions. For broader Google Ads automation, see our [Claude Skills for Google Ads](https://www.get-ryze.ai/blog/claude-skills-for-google-ads) guide.

## What are the 5 best platforms for Local Services Ads reporting?

Local Services Ads reporting requires specialized tools because standard Google Ads reports do not include lead quality metrics, call recordings, or customer lifetime value tracking. Here are the five platforms that local service businesses use most effectively, ranked by ease of setup and feature depth.

| Platform | Setup Time | Cost | Best For |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Google My Business Insights | 5 minutes | Free | Basic lead tracking |
| Ryze AI | 10 minutes | Free trial | Automated optimization |
| CallRail | 20 minutes | $30–$150/month | Call tracking specialists |
| Looker Studio | 45 minutes | Free | Custom dashboards |
| Reporting Ninja | 30 minutes | $39–$199/month | Agency-level reporting |

### Platform 1: Google My Business Insights

Google My Business Insights is the native reporting tool for Local Services Ads. It shows lead volume, customer inquiries, booking requests, and basic demographic data. The interface displays 30-day and 90-day performance windows with filters for lead type (calls vs. messages) and service categories. However, it lacks advanced metrics like lead-to-customer conversion rates and customer lifetime value calculations.

**Pros:** Free, native integration, real-time data. **Cons:** Limited customization, no call recording analysis, basic reporting only.

### Platform 2: Ryze AI

Ryze AI connects directly to your Local Services Ads account and automates bid adjustments, lead qualification scoring, and budget optimization. It tracks 18 conversion metrics including call duration, message response rate, and booking completion percentage. The platform uses machine learning to identify your most profitable lead sources and automatically adjusts your LSA profile visibility during high-conversion time windows.

**Pros:** Automated optimization, AI-powered insights, full funnel tracking. **Cons:** Subscription required after trial period.

### Platform 3: CallRail

CallRail specializes in call tracking and conversation intelligence for local businesses. It records all LSA phone calls, transcribes them using AI, and scores lead quality based on conversation content. CallRail can identify keywords that indicate high purchase intent and track which calls result in scheduled appointments. Integration with Local Services Ads requires manual setup through webhook configuration.

**Pros:** Advanced call analytics, conversation intelligence, lead scoring. **Cons:** Phone-focused only, complex setup, monthly fees scale with volume.

### Platform 4: Looker Studio

Looker Studio (formerly Google Data Studio) connects to multiple data sources including Google My Business API, Google Analytics, and third-party CRM systems to create unified Local Services Ads dashboards. You can build custom visualizations showing lead trends, cost per acquisition by service type, and conversion funnels from initial contact to paying customer. Requires technical knowledge to configure data connectors and build meaningful reports.

**Pros:** Highly customizable, multiple data sources, free forever. **Cons:** Steep learning curve, manual data mapping, no automated insights.

### Platform 5: Reporting Ninja

Reporting Ninja offers pre-built report templates specifically for Local Services Ads with drag-and-drop customization. It pulls data from Google My Business, Google Ads, and popular CRM platforms like Jobber and ServiceTitan. The platform generates weekly and monthly reports in PDF format with white-label branding options for agencies managing multiple clients.

**Pros:** Professional report design, CRM integrations, white-label options. **Cons:** Monthly subscription, limited real-time data, template-based approach.

# View reports on Local Services Ads

Local Services Ads show you reports that help you understand how your ads perform.

**On this page**

*   [Benefits](https://support.google.com/localservices/answer/6226265?hl=en#benefits)
*   [About Local Services ad reports](https://support.google.com/localservices/answer/6226265?hl=en#about)
*   [How to view your Local Services ad reports](https://support.google.com/localservices/answer/6226265?hl=en#HowTo)
*   [Local Services API](https://support.google.com/localservices/answer/6226265?hl=en#API)
*   [How to mark leads as booked](https://support.google.com/localservices/answer/6226265?hl=en#mark_leads_booked)

## Benefits

*   Track how many leads you receive from your ad.
*   Measure if those leads convert to bookings.

* * *

## About Local Services ad reports

You can select the date range for your report. The Local Services ad reports show you:

*   The number of charged leads that you received in the period from potential customers who saw your ad on Google search results pages.
*   Charged leads filtered by Category or Direct Business Search
*   A breakdown of charged leads by call, message, and booking
*   The total amount you were charged during this period
*   Total lead spend filtered by Category or Direct Business Search
*   Total lead spend broken down by call, message, and booking
*   A list of all leads received with options to filter
*   The amount of lead credits you received during this period

**Note**: Data is only available for Oct. 1, 2017 and beyond.

### How to view your Local Services ad reports

You can view your Local Services ad reports in your lead inbox. If you manage multiple businesses, you can also use the Local Services API.

1.  Open your [Local Services Ads inbox](https://ads.google.com/localservices/inbox).
2.  Select the ![Menu button](//lh3.googleusercontent.com/e0Ehm4qIlPJv8-IyHfYdXGaOoH421_cowcjrqMOV_zFRiZGd3PVMEv0QoITD3TY=w48-h48) menu at the top.
3.  Select **Reports**.

* * *

## Local Services API

Local Services API allows MCC managers to access reporting data for all their managed accounts in a scalable, programmatic way. It covers data about leads, account performance and costs. It is best suited for large companies managing multiple Local Services Ads accounts. Learn more about [how to set up API](https://developers.google.com/local-services-ads/guides/reporting).

* * *

## How to mark leads as booked

**Note:** This feature is currently only available in the U.S. and Canada.

When you mark a lead as booked, you can also add details like job type and customer name to track your leads. If you add these details you can use the filters on the Reports page to find these leads later.

1.  Open the [Local Services Ads inbox](https://ads.google.com/localservices/inbox).
2.  Choose a lead from the inbox.
3.  Select **Mark Booked** in the upper right corner.
4.  Select the date if the job is in the future, or indicate if it’s already completed.
5.  Select **Add details for tracking** to add more details about the lead, including job type and customer name. These details are only visible to you.
6.  Select **Save**.

**Note**: If you advertise through a partner affiliate, the above information doesn't apply to you. Learn more about [Partner affiliate providers](https://support.google.com/google-ads/answer/9376644).

* * *
